title: Analyser after a polariser: Malus's law
caption: Unpolarised light of 100 W m⁻² loses half at the polariser (50 W m⁻²). The analyser then transmits I = 50 cos²θ, which falls from 50 W m⁻² at 0° to zero at 90°. At 30°, I = 50 × cos²30° = 37.50000000000001 W m⁻².
alt: Graph of transmitted intensity against analyser angle from 0 to 90 degrees: a cos-squared curve from 50 watts per square metre at 0 degrees to zero at 90, passing 37.50000000000001 at 30 degrees.
description: The horizontal axis is the angle θ between the polariser and the analyser; the vertical axis is the transmitted intensity in W m⁻².
After the polariser the light is polarised with intensity 50 W m⁻², half of 100.
Malus's law gives I = 50 cos²θ: 50 at 0°, 37.50000000000001 at 30° and 0 at 90°.

checks.name: at 30° the transmitted intensity is 37.50000000000001 W m⁻²
